notes: Free edition includes 5,000 API credits per 24 hours; paid editions add capacity and features. Register an OAuth client (self-client or multi-user server application). Broad records/modules, metadata, users, activities, files, automation and notification APIs; vendor SDKs. Official hosted MCP servers cover data, customization and automation. Marketplace listing requires review; a blanket review prerequisite for independently distributed OAuth clients was not established, so public_app_review is unknown. Checked 2026-11-23.

Free Developer Edition supports development. Customer API access is included in Enterprise/Performance/Unlimited; Professional needs the Web Services API add-on. Use External Client Apps for new OAuth integrations; legacy Connected App creation is restricted. Certificate/JWT OAuth is supported. Other interface = gRPC Pub/Sub. Official hosted MCP plus DX MCP exist. AppExchange distribution has security review; a blanket review requirement for every off-marketplace OAuth distribution was not resolved. Checked 2026-11-23.

API available on all paid Helpdesk plans; start with a free trial. Converting a trial to a persistent developer sandbox requires a draft app and contacting Gorgias. Private apps use a user-linked API key sent via HTTP Basic; public apps must use OAuth2 and undergo review. Broad tickets, customers, users, tags, macros, rules, integrations and reporting resources; HTTP event hooks. Official MCP is in open beta for paid plans. Checked 2026-11-23.

Checked 2026-11-23. For a new independent developer, core Gladly/Gladly Team access must be arranged commercially; sandbox purchase is through CSM/support, with no self-serve core API trial verified. Existing customers create user-associated personal tokens using normal API User permissions (email+token Basic transport). Production requires a contracted paid instance. The separate Shopify chatbot trial does not establish core API access. Broad REST, chat SDK, appcfg CLI and webhooks. Official Gladly MCP for Claude is a closed beta requiring vendor enablement; no public OAuth client workflow documented.

Core Communications APIs: self-service signup gives key/secret and free test credit with demo restrictions; production requires funded pay-as-you-go usage/payment method (paid_plan taxonomy). Application private keys sign JWTs; CAMARA APIs also document OAuth2. Broad voice, messaging, video, verification, numbers, accounts and reporting APIs; SDKs, CLI and webhooks. Network-feature production requires operator approval; some messaging channels need registration. Official documentation and API-bindings MCP servers exist. No single vendor-wide public OAuth-app review rule verified. Checked 2026-11-23.

Checked 2026-11-23. REST uses OAuth 2; separately generated webhook tokens/API keys authorize incoming messages. API support is included on Free, with feature limits by plan. Broad resources include channels, chats, messages, users, reminders, bots and platform components; Catalyst provides Cliq SDKs. Official Zoho MCP supports Cliq. Marketplace extensions undergo review; a universal multi-customer OAuth review gate was not confirmed, so public_app_review is unknown.

Checked 2026-11-23. Scope is Marketing API. API keys for own account; OAuth for third-party customer accounts. Free accounts support API integrations within plan limits; advanced marketing features and Transactional email have separate paid requirements. Directory integrations are reviewed, but not all registered apps. Broad audiences, campaigns, templates, reports, automations, ecommerce and files interfaces, with official SDKs, mcapi CLI and webhooks. Official MCP searches documentation only; it does not access customer accounts.

Checked 2026-11-23. A free business account is available, but Pinterest reviews and may deny the initial Trial-access application before issuing app credentials; outreach_required reflects this initial vendor gate, not just public OAuth review. Standard-access upgrade is reviewed for broad customer use. Trial Pins/Boards are creator-only sandbox entities. API covers pins, boards, ads, audiences, catalogs and analytics; official Python SDK exists. Official MCP landing page still invites launch updates, so announced rather than released.

Checked 2026-11-23. FanBasis rebranded to Commas. Official SDK docs locate API keys in the seller portal and document separate sandbox/production endpoints, products, checkout sessions and transaction verification. Seller access requires onboarding and payment-partner approval, but developer sandbox provisioning, API pricing and production entitlement were not established. These unknowns do not mean no API exists. Homepage advertises MCP beta, but no usable endpoint/setup documentation was verified, so announced. No public OAuth app workflow found.

Checked 2026-11-23. Scope is merchant Commerce APIs. Self-service API keys require an eligible paid site plan: help lists Core/Plus/Advanced or legacy Commerce Advanced for Orders, Inventory and Transactions; older developer text names Commerce Advanced. Trial-key eligibility was not explicitly confirmed. OAuth clients need vendor review; approved Extensions can connect customers on any site plan. Broad commerce resources and OAuth-only webhook subscriptions. Official remote MCP offers anonymous domain tools and authenticated commerce tools.

Checked 2026-11-23. Direct API v3 uses self-created API keys and requires a paid plan; general API use and remote MCP start at Lite. Free test queries still require a paid account. Connect OAuth requires an eligibility application and production verification; its approval page says Enterprise for new integrations, while the API help page says Lite+ activation, so confirm that commercial-app tier. Verdict uses the direct paid API route. Broad SEO, keywords, audit, ranking, brand, analytics and management APIs include resource writes. Current v3 is active; v2 is retired.

Checked 2026-11-23. API keys are self-service; native proxy access additionally uses a provisioned username/password. Current Web Scraper/SERP and MCP offerings have recurring free quotas; usage beyond quotas and other products require payment. Broad web search, scraping, browser, datasets, proxy/configuration and account-management interfaces; official SDKs and CLI plus webhook delivery; other denotes native proxy/browser protocols. Official local and hosted MCP are published by Bright Data. No public third-party OAuth app workflow found.

Reviewed 2026-11-23. Self-service trial lasts 30 days or until credits are exhausted; ongoing production requires a paid account/usage billing. Auth: OAuth, programmatic access tokens (mapped to personal_token), key-pair JWT, and workload identity federation (other). Broad SQL/resource APIs, SDKs, CLI, and JDBC/ODBC (api_types other); outbound webhooks support only documented destination services. Custom OAuth is configured by the customer's account, without a documented vendor publication review. Official managed MCP is available; trial AI features require adding a credit card.

Reviewed 2026-11-23. Current pricing explicitly includes API and third-party integrations from Team upward and offers a 14-day Business trial. An API tutorial recommends a free Developer account, conflicting with pricing; paid production is the confirmed advertised route. Free-plan MCP access is separately advertised. Auth supports OAuth2, personal tokens and organization integration tokens (other, not deprecated API keys). Broad organizations/projects/teams/issues/releases/monitoring APIs. Public integrations require Sentry publication approval; this alone does not drive the verdict.

Reviewed 2026-11-23. All accounts, including free and trial accounts, include API access. Free plan has one active person and two active projects; paid features remain gated (e.g. data imports). PATs are self-created; OAuth apps are self-registered with no vendor review step in documented authorization. API v2 covers clients, projects, time entries, tasks, expenses, invoices, estimates, users and reports. Current auth is OAuth2/PAT; legacy v1 Basic auth is excluded. Official remote Harvest MCP is documented for Free and paid plans.

Reviewed 2026-11-23. Web API is available on all plans; Free permits 1,000 calls/workspace/month and 5 requests/second/base. Authentication uses PATs or OAuth; legacy API keys no longer work. OAuth sharing requires policy/terms URLs and support email, without a vendor review step in the documented process. Resource coverage includes records/comments, bases/tables/fields, webhooks, users and enterprise administration; enterprise operations require eligible plans. Official JavaScript client, Blocks SDK/CLI and webhooks exist. Official MCP is available on all plans under the same permissions and API limits.

Checked 2026-11-23. A candidate official Paygent homepage names Paygent Connect and advertises REST/SDK/webhooks and sandbox access. Its relationship to the supplied NMI-powered hint and working credential documentation could not be verified. Do not attribute unrelated Japanese Paygent or AI-wallet products to this row. Authentication uses unknown under the guide's time-box fallback. Third-party audit snippets surfaced during identity searches and were excluded from the evidence.

Reviewed 2026-11-23. Free developer account/demo company; real production organisations need a Xero subscription. Developer Starter is free for up to 5 connections; larger commercial use needs paid tiers. Since March 2026, Core allows 50 connections; Plus and above require certification, with security/use-case gates for certain advanced APIs. OAuth2 covers standard apps and optional paid Custom Connections; no API-key route. Broad accounting APIs plus SDKs/webhooks. Official remote MCP is available on Core+ for live organisations, Starter for demo only. Review is recorded separately; paid production/tier needs drive the verdict.

Checked 2026-11-23. Scope is the Enterprise API, now branded Gemini Notebook Enterprise, not the consumer app. Docs require a licensed user and user OAuth credentials; generic service-account support was not assumed. Self-service 14-day full-featured trial; paid subscriptions have a 15-license minimum. Ordinary project IAM and license assignment are not vendor approval. Three documented resource families: notebooks, sources and audio overviews. Guide pages label these APIs Preview. No first-party NotebookLM MCP server verified; Gemini Enterprise's external-MCP client support is separate. Public OAuth review unresolved.

Checked 2026-11-23. API keys and webhooks are included on all plans; OAuth supports customer integrations. User-scoped access covers owned/shared meetings, never others' private meetings. Core meeting data is read-oriented: meetings, transcripts, summaries and downloads; documented writes manage webhooks/export jobs, not meeting content, so limited under the supplied rubric. Teams/users and webhook resources make breadth moderate. Official TypeScript/Python SDKs and vendor MCP exist. Public OAuth docs mention review but do not clearly establish a mandatory pre-distribution gate; marketplace featuring is separate.
